To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the combined genotype of A(TA)nTAA (n = 6 or 7) and –3279T or –3279G decreases UGT1A expression by CAR, PNR, or GR but increases UGT1A mRNA expression by HNF4α in human liver.
the combined genotypes of A(TA)nTAA in the RNA polymerases II core promoter and –3279T>GG in PBREM of the UGT gene affect the transcription of the UGT enzyme by the transcription factors.
the genetic polymorphsims in the RNA polymeras II core promoter and PBREM have combined effects on transcription mediated by CAR or PXR but not by GR.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the combined effects of the genetic polymorphs of the UGT 1A1 TAT A box and PBREM on UGT1 A1 transcription in human liver.
the combined effects of the genetic polymorphims in the RNA polymeras II core promoter and upstream PBREM of the UGT 1A1 promoter on UGT1 A1 transcription.
the combined effects of genetic polymorphisms of the UGT 1A1 promoter on transcription of UGT1A mediated by the transcriptional factors.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the combined effects of genetic polymorphisms of the UGT promoter on the transcription mediated by CAR and PXR are more complex than previously anticipated and that the genetic polymorphims in the UGT promoter have combined effects that are different from the effects of the individual genetic polymorphisms.
the genetic polymorphsims in the TATA box and PBREM of the UGTIA1 promoter have combined effect on UGTIA1 transcription mediated by CAR,PXR,or GR.
the combined genotypes of TA7 plus –327G and TA6 plus –327G have a combined negative effect on the transcription mediated by CAR and PXR, but not by GR, HNF4, or HNF1α.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the combined genotypes of A(TA)nTAA and –3280G/G decrease the transcription of UGT1A mediated by CAR, but not PXR or GR, and the combined genotype of A(TA6/7)TAA and – 3279G/G decrease UGT1 A transcription mediated by CAR or PXR, but not GR.
the combined genotypes of the UGTIA1 polymorphisms decrease UGT1AI expression and function, and thus, the combined genotypers are associated with the risk of bilirubin toxicity and/or drug toxicity.

genetic polymorphisms of the UGT 1A1 promoter can affect the transcriptional regulation by CAR, P XR, or GR, which may lead to interindividual variability of UGT1A-mediated drug metabolism and/or drug-drug interactions.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the genetic polymorphims in the UGTIA1 promoter can alter the transcription mediated by CAR or PXR.
the genetic polymorphsisms in the UGT promoter have combined effects to alter UGT transcription.

genetic polymorphisms can alter UGT1A expression in a combined manner, which should be taken into consideration when studying the effects of genetic polymorphisms on drug metabolism and drug-induced liver injury.
